Lemma
[vanishing from a Lipschitz differential inequality] Source: cao-zhu 1. Lemma 2.3.2\group Cao–Zhu Advanced Maximum Principle for Tensors Suppose $\varphi : [a,b]\rightarrow \mathbb {R}$ is Lipschitz continuous and suppose for some constant $C<+\infty $, \begin{align*} & \frac{d}{dt}\varphi (t)\le C\varphi (t),\quad whenever\ \varphi (t)\ge 0\; \ on\ \; [a,b),\\[2mm] \text{and}\hskip28.452755905511808pt& \varphi (a)\le 0. \end{align*} Then $\varphi (t)\le 0$ on $[a,b]$.

Proof

\sketch After multiplying by $e^{-Ct}$, compare with $\varepsilon (t-a)$ and let $\varepsilon \to 0$.

□
